issues.quote: This script does not run directly on your computer; you start it from your terminal, and it runs inside the example system that `scripts/up.sh` started
issues.text: I can follow the instruction (start the system first), but "not on your computer" and "from your terminal" pull against each other, and later "`143` is what the script reports for that kind of stop inside the example system, where it always runs" hints the number could differ elsewhere. I accept it and move on; nothing in the main idea or the quiz depends on it.
issues.fix: Replace "does not run directly on your computer" with "is handed over by your terminal to the example system", so the two halves of the sentence no longer contradict each other.

issues.quote: a tool that lists the runs on the same machine, like `ps` in the script below does inside the example system, lists each run by that kind of number
issues.text: I re-read this twice: "like `ps` ... does" breaks the grammar of the sentence, and the aside sits in the middle of an already long paragraph about the C# sample.
issues.fix: Split it: "A tool that lists the runs on the same machine lists each run by that kind of number; `ps`, in the script below, is one."

issues.quote: A tool that lists the runs on the same machine would list this run under the same number the sample prints
issues.text: Options (e) and (a) are near-verbatim from the lesson ("a tool that lists the runs on the same machine ... lists each run by that kind of number"; "the same one on every run started the same way"), so I matched wording rather than reasoning. Also the stem says "what one run of it would print" but (a) and (d) compare two runs.
issues.fix: Reword the stem to "Predict what runs of it would print" and paraphrase (e), e.g. "`ps`, asked about this run, would show the number the sample printed as `process id`".

issues.quote: Only that `sleep` had no say in the number — something else ended the run for it
issues.text: In q4 and q5 the correct answer is the cautious, hedged option ("Nothing certain...", "Only that..."), while the distractors all assert something firm. By q5 I could pick it from tone alone.
issues.fix: Make one distractor in q5 hedged too, e.g. "Only that `sleep` failed at its own work", so tone no longer marks the answer.
